spreads.title: History of the Rosary & How to Use This Book

left_page.heading: The History of the Holy Rosary
left_page.subheading: Origins of the Gospel Prayer of the Church

sections.title: Monastic Roots & The Marian Psalter
sections.body: The roots of the Rosary reach back to the early centuries of the Church, when monks prayed all 150 Psalms of David each week. For the faithful and lay brothers who could not read Latin manuscripts, a devotion arose of reciting 150 Pater Nosters (Our Fathers), and later 150 Ave Marias (Hail Marys), counted on cords of knotted beads known as 'Paternosters.' Known as the 'Psalter of the Blessed Virgin Mary,' this practice allowed every believer to unite their daily work and prayer to the liturgical rhythm of the Church.

sections.title: St. Dominic & Preaching the Mysteries
sections.body: In the thirteenth century, tradition holds that the Blessed Virgin Mary entrusted the Rosary to St. Dominic de Guzmán (1170–1221) as a spiritual remedy against heresy—uniting vocal prayer with quiet meditation on the saving events of Christ's life, death, and resurrection. In the fifteenth century, the Carthusian monk Dominic of Prussia and the Dominican friar Blessed Alan de la Roche organized the Marian Psalter into fifteen decades, each paired with a specific Gospel mystery.

sections.title: Pope St. Pius V & The Twenty Mysteries
sections.body: In 1569, Pope St. Pius V formally established the traditional form of the fifteen Joyful, Sorrowful, and Glorious Mysteries in his papal bull Consueverunt Romani Pontifices, and in 1571 instituted the feast of Our Lady of Victory (renamed the Feast of Our Lady of the Rosary in 1573). More than four centuries later, in his 2002 Apostolic Letter Rosarium Virginis Mariae, Pope St. John Paul II enriched this heritage by introducing the five Luminous Mysteries (the Mysteries of Light), inviting Christians to contemplate the public ministry of Christ from His Baptism in the Jordan to the Institution of the Eucharist.

right_page.heading: Structure of the Book & How to Pray
right_page.subheading: Praying with Scripture, Prayer, and Sacred Art

sections.title: How This Book Is Organized
sections.body:
Every prayer section and Mystery in this book is designed as a single, self-contained two-page spread so you never need to flip back and forth while praying:
• Left Page (Word & Prayer): Displays the Mystery title, its spiritual fruit, a passage from Sacred Scripture, a brief meditation, and the complete prayers for that decade.
• Right Page (Visual Contemplation): Displays the Mystery header at the top and a framed Renaissance or Baroque masterpiece to rest your eyes and heart upon as you pray the ten Hail Marys.
• Six Index Tabs (O, J, L, S, G, C): Grab any tab on the right and flip it to the left to open directly to the Opening Prayers (O), Joyful (J), Luminous (L), Sorrowful (S), or Glorious (G) Mysteries, or the Closing Prayers (C).

sections.title: Step-by-Step Guide to Praying the Rosary
sections.body:
1. Opening Prayers (Tab O): Make the Sign of the Cross, pray the Apostles' Creed on the Crucifix, the Our Father on the first large bead, three Hail Marys (for Faith, Hope, and Charity) on the three small beads, and the Glory Be.
2. The Five Decades (Tabs J, L, S, G): Flip the tab for the day's Mystery set to the left. Read the Scripture and meditation, pray one Our Father, ten Hail Marys while contemplating the Mystery and artwork, one Glory Be, and the Fatima Prayer. Proceed through all five decades of that Mystery set.
3. Closing Prayers (Tab C): Flip Tab C to the left and conclude with the Hail, Holy Queen (Salve Regina), the Concluding Rosary Prayer, and the Sign of the Cross.

sections.title: Weekly Schedule of the Mysteries
sections.body:
• Joyful Mysteries (Tab J): Monday & Saturday (and Sundays of Advent & Christmas)
• Luminous Mysteries (Tab L): Thursday
• Sorrowful Mysteries (Tab S): Tuesday & Friday (and Sundays of Lent)
• Glorious Mysteries (Tab G): Wednesday & Sunday (in Easter & Ordinary Time)

epigraph.quote: The Rosary, though clearly Marian in character, is at heart a Christocentric prayer. In the sobriety of its elements, it has all the depth of the Gospel message in its entirety, of which it can be said to be a compendium.
epigraph.attribution: Pope St. John Paul II, Rosarium Virginis Mariae (2002)

back_cover.synopsis: Designed so that you never need to turn a page mid-decade, Pray the Rosary pairs the complete prayers, Sacred Scripture passages, and spiritual fruits of all twenty Mysteries on the left-hand page with twenty-three breathtaking Renaissance and Baroque masterworks on the right-hand page. Whether used for quiet personal contemplation, family prayer, or learning the Rosary for the first time, this volume invites you to gaze upon the face of Christ with the heart of His Blessed Mother.

marian_counsel.quote: Never will anyone who says his Rosary every day become a formal heretic or be led astray by the devil. This is a statement that I would gladly sign with my blood.
marian_counsel.attribution: St. Louis Marie de Montfort, The Secret of the Rosary
